meta.note: Do not confuse policy intention with actual law. Each instrument is typed as LAW / REGULATION / POLICY / STRATEGY / PROPOSAL / GOVERNMENT STATEMENT / INDUSTRY POSITION. Statuses move through: Proposed > Draft > Public Comment > Under Review > Approved > Gazetted > Commenced > Operational > Superseded. Verify the latest consolidated text via SAFLII, Juta, or the Government Printing Works before relying on any clause. This tracker is intelligence, not legal advice.

instruments.title: National Road Traffic Act 93 of 1996
instruments.significance: Primary road traffic statute: vehicle standards, roadworthiness, driver obligations, road rules, licensing. Contains NO comprehensive automated driving regime. Under the current text an operator-driver obligation framework applies to vehicles driven on a public road.
instruments.avGap: No framework for L3+ without a human driver in control; no certification path for automated driving systems; testing regime effectively unspecified.

evidence.claim: National Road Traffic Act 93 of 1996 is the operative road traffic law of South Africa.

instruments.title: National Road Traffic Regulations, 2000 (as amended)
instruments.significance: Operational detail under the NRTA: road rules, vehicle registration, roadworthiness, dimensions/mass, traffic signs.
instruments.avGap: No automated-driving licence or ADS-equipment regime.

evidence.claim: Regulations pursuant to the NRTA govern road rules and vehicle standards.
evidence.note: Verify specific Government Notice number and latest amendment.

instruments.title: Road Traffic Management Corporation Act 20 of 1999
instruments.significance: RTMC: implements the NRTA, manages the National Crash Database / crash data, and coordinates road traffic law enforcement, driver licensing, and road safety programmes. Key institutional partner for crash data ingestion.
instruments.avGap: Crash data is the single highest-value dataset for autonomy safety modelling; formal data-sharing with AV testing is not established.

evidence.claim: RTMC is the implementation agency for the NRTA and custodian of national road traffic data.

instruments.title: SANRAL Act 7 of 1998
instruments.significance: National roads agency; owns/operates the national toll & freeway network; partner for corridor pilots and digital-road-twin data.
instruments.avGap: Road/traffic data product ecosystem is nascent.

evidence.claim: SANRAL manages the national road network.

instruments.title: National Land Transport Act 5 of 2009
instruments.significance: Public transport planning and operating licences (bus, taxi, shuttle); governs any public-transport pilot including autonomous shuttles operating as public transport.
instruments.avGap: No category for an autonomous public-transport operator; permits assume a licensed driver operator.

evidence.claim: The NLTA regulates public transport operating licences.

instruments.title: National Land Transport Strategic Framework
instruments.statusNote: Prior framework cycles (e.g. NLTSF 2017–2022) largely elapsed; successor framework status must be verified.
instruments.significance: Sets public-transport and mobility priorities; mobility-as-a-service and pilot language may be found here.
instruments.avGap: Does not constitute law; position/priority only.

evidence.claim: NLTSF is a policy framework, not legislation.

instruments.title: DoT priority: legislative framework for autonomous vehicle technology
instruments.statusNote: Department of Transport has previously identified development of a legislative framework for autonomous vehicle technology as a priority. Treat as evidence of direction and of possible upcoming consultation, NOT as enacted law.
instruments.significance: If converted into formal regulation, this becomes the trigger condition for public-road testing/deployment. Its absence is currently the single largest legal blocker for public-road autonomy.
instruments.avGap: Primary blocker: no gazetted automated-driving instrument exists (as at the state of knowledge in this tracker).

evidence.claim: Development of a legislative framework for autonomous vehicle technology has been identified as a priority by the Department of Transport.
evidence.source: Client operational brief + DoT public statements
evidence.note: Locate the authoritative DoT pronouncement/document and track to gazette.

instruments.title: Electric Vehicles White Paper (dtic)
instruments.statusNote: Published December 2023 by the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition.
instruments.significance: Policy direction toward new-energy vehicles and localisation; supports the electrification-autonomy convergence logic.
instruments.avGap: White paper is policy intent, not a binding levy/tariff regime.

evidence.claim: An Electric Vehicles White Paper was published by the dtic in December 2023.
evidence.publisher: Department of Trade, Industry and Competition
evidence.note: Verify final gazetted status and subsequent implementation decisions.

instruments.title: Automotive Production Development Programme (APDP) 2021–2035
instruments.significance: Localisation incentives framework for vehicle/component production; vehicle-built localisation and NEV support may be extended toward electronic/software components.
instruments.avGap: Autonomy-specific components not separately incentivised (verify current qualification criteria).

evidence.claim: APDP is South Africa's automotive incentive framework (phase II to 2035).

instruments.title: Protection of Personal Information Act 4 of 2013 (POPIA)
instruments.significance: Governs collection of camera/telematics/personal data for datasets and fleet analytics. Any SA driving dataset, dashcam program, or behaviour research must be POPIA-compliant (lawful basis, purpose limitation, de-identification).
instruments.avGap: Clean-data licensing and de-identification workflows are not standard in the SA AV industry.

evidence.claim: POPIA is in force and regulates processing of personal information in South Africa.

instruments.title: Cybercrimes Act 19 of 2020
instruments.significance: Cyber-physical vehicle/back-end attacks engage this statute; fleet security incidents have criminal-law consequences.
instruments.avGap: No automotive-sector-specific cybersecurity standards are gazetted; ISO/SAE 21434 alignment is voluntary.

evidence.claim: Cybercrimes Act in force since December 2021.

instruments.title: Electronic Communications and Transactions Act 25 of 2002
instruments.significance: Framework for electronic transactions/signatures; minor relevance to remote operations and telemetry contracting.

instruments.title: Consumer Protection Act 68 of 2008
instruments.significance: Product-liability-adjacent consumer protections relevant to personal AV/ADAS offerings.

instruments.title: Administrative Adjudication of Road Traffic Offences Act 46 of 1998 (AARTO)
instruments.statusNote: Partially commenced and legally contested. Constitutional Court / SCA challenges (2022–2023) flagged defects (e.g. Oosthuizen v Minister). Status and rollout remain in flux.
instruments.significance: Affects traffic enforcement architecture and how infringement (incl. potential automated-driving oversight) is adjudicated.
instruments.avGap: Enforcement regime instability complicates liability/penalty design for automated operations.

evidence.claim: AARTO is partially commenced and subject to appellate rulings.
evidence.source: Act text + SCA/CC rulings (Mokoena, Oosthuizen cases report)

instruments.title: National Road Safety Strategy (RSA 2016–2030 and revisions)
instruments.statusNote: Under revision toward post-2030 targets; monitor.
instruments.significance: Contains targets around crash reduction; provides a policy hook to frame autonomy as a safety intervention rather than a novelty.

evidence.claim: National road safety strategy documents exist; revision status must be verified.
